title: Staff found the Kalmykian president missing from his room

tellings.quote: >> This is what's crazy. I have his staff on record being like, "We went into his room, his clothes were missing, and we couldn't find him anywhere.
My friends were already in the apartment looking for me for over an hour and couldn't find me.
tellings.difference: Told firsthand and placed in a Moscow apartment in September 1997. It is his friends, not his staff, who search for over an hour, and he then reappears from the bedroom. The story says Kalmykia and mentions missing clothes.
tellings.link_reason: The same disappearance: people searched his rooms for him and could not find him. This matches the story of the Kalmykian president's staff finding him missing.

as_told.title: Friends search the apartment and he reappears from the bedroom

tellings.quote: Then some time passed, maybe an hour, and suddenly he appears from the bedroom, even though he wasn't there before.
tellings.difference: Told firsthand by Vasili, dated September 17, 1997, in Moscow. It adds that he reappeared from the bedroom after about an hour.
tellings.link_reason: An associate's firsthand account of the same vanishing and reappearance, matching the staff-search story.

as_told.title: Associate's account of Kirsan vanishing and reappearing

plain: The president of Kalmykia, a small republic inside Russia, is said to have vanished from a locked room for about an hour and then reappeared. He has called this being taken by aliens. The president, Kiran Ilum Xenov, tells it himself. He places it in a Moscow apartment in September 1997. He says his friends "were already in the apartment looking for me for over an hour and couldn't find me." A witness named Vasili, who says he was there, dates it to September 17, 1997. He says that after maybe an hour "he appears from the bedroom, even though he wasn't there before." Michels tells it a little differently. He says he has the president's staff on record saying they went into his room, "his clothes were missing, and we couldn't find him anywhere." He also cites the chess champion Garry Kasparov. If true, it would mean a sitting head of a region physically disappeared during a contact experience.
